then R, knitr, TinyTeX, and the bibliography pipeline all work. Sentinel: `CHF-CHECK-R-OK`.

## An equation

The household maximises utility subject to a full-income constraint:

$$
\max_{x,\,\ell}\; u(x, \ell) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad p\,x = w\,(T - \ell) + v,
$$ {#eq-budget}

and @eq-budget is referred to here by its label, so cross-references work too.

## A figure (ggplot2)

```{r}
#| label: fig-check
#| fig-cap: "Fuel economy against weight, example data shipped with R."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.5
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73"), name = "Cylinders") +
  labs(x = "Weight (1000 lb)", y = "Miles per gallon") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## A regression table (fixest + modelsummary)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-check
#| tbl-cap: "Two specifications, example data."
library(fixest)
library(modelsummary)
m1 <- feols(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
m2 <- feols(mpg ~ wt + hp | cyl, data = mtcars)
modelsummary(list("OLS" = m1, "Cylinder FE" = m2),
             stars = TRUE, gof_map = c("nobs", "r.squared"),
             notes = "Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors in parentheses.",
             vcov = "HC1", output = "latex")
```
